minutes.headline: Board approved the Arrow Estates subdivision decision with a cap of 25 building permits per 365 days.
minutes.summary: The board reorganized, approved two ANR plans and a common-driveway location, and heard a farm owner ask about public water and sewer on Chase Road. It heard Unitil on tree work on scenic roads and approved a de minimis tree change for the settler solar project. After a long deliberation it approved the Arrow Estates decision as amended, then filled most committee seats and tabled the rest of the agenda.

public_comment.topic: The superintendent said the school department is watching town developments for their effect on schools, budget and services.
Applicant's attorney asked for longer construction hours on Saturdays and weekday starts at seven.
Applicant said he needs a firm phasing number for his bank and then agreed to 25 all-inclusive.

Board and applicant discussed a cap on annual permits, with the applicant first offering 25 non-age-restricted plus 11 age-restricted.
Unitil said an independent consultant paid by ratepayers would need a prudency review.

decisions.decision: Board agreed to schedule a workshop on infrastructure and economic development, prompted by the Chase Road farm request.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board approved the Arrow Estates subdivision decision as amended, including a cap on building permits in any 365-day period, all-inclusive.
The applicant said he needs a firm phasing number for his bank, then agreed to the all-inclusive cap after the board worked through the other conditions first.
The board voted to schedule a workshop on infrastructure and potential economic development, prompted by a Chase Road farm owner's request about public water and sewer.
Unitil briefed the board on tree work on scenic roads and will return in about three weeks with detail on one section for a public hearing.
The board approved a de minimis tree change for the settler solar project, with one abstention, and filled most committee seats before tabling the rest of the agenda.

why_it_matters: The permit cap sets how fast new homes at Arrow Estates can be built, which shapes the pace of added demand on schools, roads and town services.
The infrastructure workshop and Unitil's scenic-road tree work could lead to later decisions on public water and sewer and on roadside trees, which would come to residents through public hearings.
watch_next: Unitil's return to the board in about three weeks, with detail on one road section for a public hearing.
